I looked at the two “broken” screenshots and the CSS grammar in components/prism-css.js. In the “actual” image you can see that Prism is stopping the URL tokenization at the first colon (`:`) inside the quoted URL, so the rest of the URL is being tokenized as punctuation, plain text, functions, etc., instead of staying inside the same quoted‐string.  

Root cause: the original `url`‐rule’s regex is too brittle for quoted URLs containing colons, semicolons, ampersands, etc. It splits on those characters rather than treating the entire quoted block as one string.  

The fix is to replace the existing `url` pattern (and its accompanying “inside” string) with a single, self‐contained regex literal that:

 • matches `url(`  
 • then any amount of whitespace  
 • then either a single‐ or double‐quoted string (with proper backslash escapes) or any sequence of characters up to the closing `)`  
 • then any amount of whitespace  
 • and finally the closing `)`  

Below are two *SEARCH/REPLACE* patches—one for the unminified and one for the minified build—that swap out the old `RegExp(...)` construction for a cleaner `/\burl\(\s*(?:(?:"[^"]*"|'[^']*')|[^)])*\s*\)/i` literal (plus the matching “inside”‐string regex).

Based on the screenshots and the code in your snippets, the problem is that in the URL‐inside rule we wrap the two alternative string‐patterns in `^`…`$` without grouping, so the anchors only apply to the first alternative.  In practice that means only part of your quoted URL (up to the first “|” in the alternation) is actually seen as a string, and the rest falls back to other tokens (colon, function, punctuation, etc.).  

The fix is simply to wrap the entire `string.source` alternation in a non‐capturing group when we add the `^` and `$`.  Below are two *SEARCH/REPLACE* edits—one for the normal file and one for the minified file—that make this change.
